A1.justification: Both complete PDFs describe PipeOffload. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–E support reliable comparison, including matching renumbered appendix figures.

before.justification: v1 reports original GPU experiments measuring activation memory, throughput, offload overhead, scaling, and memory-transfer stability.

after.justification: v2 retains those experiments and adds comparisons with memory-saving baselines and a training-loss convergence experiment.

M1.justification: The selective-offload strategy, GIS/GIS-H schedules, PO-H/PO-F variants, and offload implementation remain unchanged. The added experiments evaluate existing methods.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate GPT-3-like language-model training. The added comparisons and convergence check introduce no identified dataset, domain, or task; model configurations and diagnostic measurements change within existing coverage.

E2.justification: Section 5.5 and Figure 12 add evaluated comparisons against V-Min, V-Half, and activation-rematerialized 1F1B-I, labeled 1F1B-I-R. This substantially broadens comparison beyond the standard pipeline schedules to alternatives specifically targeting activation memory; v1 discussed V-shaped schedules without evaluating them.

E3.justification: Section 5.6 adds loss-versus-iteration evaluation of PO-H, PO-F, and 1F1B-I on a 5.4B model using eight GPUs, plotted over approximately 1,000 iterations. Figure 12 also reports specified model/GPU/sequence configurations for the additional comparisons. Existing experimental settings and metrics are retained.

E4.justification: Figure 13 adds a convergence check testing whether the offload implementations preserve the baseline loss trajectory. Existing offload, recomputation, scaling, and topology analyses remain, including their appendix evidence.

E5.justification: Appendix D retains its description of repeated transfer experiments and Table 3's bandwidth distributions. The added experiments introduce no reported seed counts, confidence intervals, significance tests, or new uncertainty-estimation practice.

E6.justification: Figure 12 adds memory–throughput results against the new baselines across four configurations, supporting favorable Pareto trade-offs for the proposed schedules. Figure 13 adds nearly identical loss trajectories for PO-H, PO-F, and 1F1B-I. Together these substantially extend comparative and correctness evidence; the original performance figures and appendix numerical values are retained.

T1.justification: Equation 1, the schedule-memory and bubble expressions in Section 3, and Table 1 remain unchanged. The new empirical correctness discussion supplies no formal proof or revised mathematical assumption.

C1.justification: The abstract and conclusion retain the same contributions: better-than-linear selective offload, improved pipeline memory scaling, and up to 19% acceleration relative to tensor-parallel configurations. Introduction edits clarify existing reasoning without changing these claims.

C2.justification: Section 5.5 newly attributes V-shaped schedules' weaker performance to unequal forward, activation-gradient, and weight-gradient timings violating their approximate-equality assumption. Section 5.6 interprets loss agreement as correctness evidence and states that the methods are exact. Existing offload caveats remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Section 4 and Appendices C–D retain the same buffer management, recomputation, synchronization, hardware, and node-assignment details. The code-access link is unchanged. Beyond basic evaluation settings, the added experiments provide no new implementation or reproduction instructions.

R1.justification: The reference set and Related Work discussion are retained. New Section 5.5 adds focused positioning against Qi et al. (2024)'s V-shaped schedules and activation rematerialization, including a critique of the former's timing assumption.

P1.justification: v2 makes localized introduction edits, changes author ordering, adds experimental subsections 5.5–5.6 and a generic Impact Statement, and includes publication information. Most existing prose and the overall section sequence remain unchanged.

P2.justification: v2 adds the four-panel Pareto comparison in Figure 12 and loss curves in Figure 13, with accompanying text reflow and appendix-figure renumbering. Table 3's synchronized dual-stream sketch is realigned. Existing plots and table structures are otherwise retained.

improvement.justification: The added memory-saving baselines and convergence check strengthen empirical support beyond v1's efficiency comparisons. The gains are limited by sparse documentation of the new experiments and convergence evidence from one model configuration; Figure 13's claim of proving algorithmic correctness exceeds what matching loss curves establish.
